\chapter{Welcomes, Gifts, Invitations}
\label{ch:te-welcomes-gifts}
\hlchaptermodality{99}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can greet with namaste, say I am delighted to see someone, congratulate, and talk about gifts and invitations.}

Complete TE-R99-second-pass-welcome: short answers and a warm welcome, from cold.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[namastē]{\te{నమస్తే} (namastē) — namaste, hello}

\label{lesson:TE-C99-namaste}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for that's true, then the Telugu for that's the one.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{నమస్తే}}
\textbf{\te{నమస్తే}} (\emph{namastē}) — \textquotedblleft{}namaste\textquotedblright{}, said with the palms together.

It sits beside \textbf{\te{నమస్కారం}}, your first word. Both bow: \textbf{\te{నమస్తే}} is \textquotedblleft{}a bow to you\textquotedblright{}, heard all across India; \textbf{\te{నమస్కారం}} is the fuller Telugu form.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second hello, shared with most of India.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{namastē}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{namastē}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{namastē}, then \emph{namaskāraṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for that's true, then the Telugu for that's the one, then say \emph{namastē} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{నమస్తే} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Namaste, hello\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ānandaṁ]{\te{ఆనందం} (ānandaṁ) — delight, joy}

\label{lesson:TE-C99-delight}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for that's the one, then the Telugu for namaste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఆనందం}}
\textbf{\te{ఆనందం}} (\emph{ānandaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}delight, joy\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మిమ్మల్ని} \te{చూసి} \te{ఆనందంగా} \te{ఉంది}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am delighted to see you\textquotedblright{}. Stronger than \textbf{\te{సంతోషం}}, and in the frame you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A warmer word for glad.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ānandaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ānandaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mimmalni cūsi ānandaṁgā undi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for that's the one, then the Telugu for namaste, then say \emph{ānandaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఆనందం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Delight, joy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[abhinandanalu]{\te{అభినందనలు} (abhinandanalu) — congratulations, compliments}

\label{lesson:TE-C99-congrats}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for namaste, then the Telugu for delight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అభినందనలు}}
\textbf{\te{అభినందనలు}} (\emph{abhinandanalu}) — \textquotedblleft{}congratulations\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}compliments\textquotedblright{} on something done well.

\textbf{\te{శుభాకాంక్షలు}} wishes someone well for what is coming; \textbf{\te{అభినందనలు}} praises what they have done. A passed exam gets both.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Praise for what is done, beside wishes for what comes.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanalu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abhinandanalu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{abhinandanalu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for namaste, then the Telugu for delight, then say \emph{abhinandanalu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అభినందనలు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Congratulations, compliments\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bahumati]{\te{బహుమతి} (bahumati) — a gift, a prize}

\label{lesson:TE-C99-gift}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for delight, then the Telugu for congratulations.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{బహుమతి}}
\textbf{\te{బహుమతి}} (\emph{bahumati}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}a prize\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{ఒక} \te{బహుమతి}} — \textquotedblleft{}a gift for you\textquotedblright{}, with the dative \textbf{\te{మీకు}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Something to bring when you visit.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahumati}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahumati}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mīku oka bahumati}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for delight, then the Telugu for congratulations, then say \emph{bahumati} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{బహుమతి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A gift, a prize\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[āhvānaṁ]{\te{ఆహ్వానం} (āhvānaṁ) — an invitation}

\label{lesson:TE-C99-invitation}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for congratulations, then the Telugu for a gift.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఆహ్వానం}}
\textbf{\te{ఆహ్వానం}} (\emph{āhvānaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{పెళ్ళికి} \te{ఆహ్వానం}} — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation to the wedding\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{-\te{కి}}, \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{}. It is the reason for most of the visits this book has taught you to make.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Namaste, delight, congratulations, a gift, an invitation: the way into a visit.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āhvānaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āhvānaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{peḷḷiki āhvānaṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for congratulations, then the Telugu for a gift, then say \emph{āhvānaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఆహ్వానం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An invitation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{A warm welcome and short answers — a second pass}

\label{lesson:TE-R99-second-pass-welcome}



\begin{quote}
A friend arrives at your door. Greet them with palms together, and say you are delighted.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the ending -\te{ఏ}, \textquotedblleft{}exactly this\textquotedblright{}}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{built from} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\te{నిజమే}} & truth + -\te{ఏ} \\
\textbf{\te{అదే}} & that + -\te{ఏ} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

The \textbf{-\te{ఏ}} points: \emph{this truth and no other}, \emph{that one exactly}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item hand over a gift; congratulate your friend
  \item say the wedding invitation came
  \item someone asks what happened: it's nothing. Have you eaten? Not yet
  \item agree that it's true; say that will do; and \textquotedblleft{}that's the one!\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Nothing? (\textbf{\te{ఏమీ} \te{లేదు}}.) Not yet? (\textbf{\te{ఇంకా} \te{లేదు}}.) That will do? (\textbf{\te{సరిపోతుంది}}.) That's true? (\textbf{\te{నిజమే}}.) That's the one? (\textbf{\te{అదే}}.) Namaste? (\textbf{\te{నమస్తే}}.) Delight? (\textbf{\te{ఆనందం}}.) Congratulations? (\textbf{\te{అభినందనలు}}.) A gift? (\textbf{\te{బహుమతి}}.) An invitation? (\textbf{\te{ఆహ్వానం}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Who you are and how you are — a second pass}

\label{lesson:TE-R99-second-pass-names-moods}



\begin{quote}
Give your surname first, then your nickname, then ask someone their age.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a name in two parts}]
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{literally} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\te{ఇంటిపేరు}} & house name \\
\textbf{\te{ముద్దుపేరు}} & affection name \\
\textbf{\te{పుట్టినరోజు}} & born day \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Each is built from pieces you know, and the house name goes first.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item wish someone a happy birthday; hand them a gift
  \item ask them to sign here
  \item tell a friend to smile; then say you felt like crying
  \item tell a worried friend not to worry; say you regret it; say you are alone
  \item say an invitation came
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A surname? (\textbf{\te{ఇంటిపేరు}}.) A nickname? (\textbf{\te{ముద్దుపేరు}}.) Age? (\textbf{\te{వయసు}}.) A birthday? (\textbf{\te{పుట్టినరోజు}}.) A signature? (\textbf{\te{సంతకం}}.) A laugh? (\textbf{\te{నవ్వు}}.) Crying? (\textbf{\te{ఏడుపు}}.) Regret? (\textbf{\te{విచారం}}.) Worry? (\textbf{\te{ఆందోళన}}.) Alone? (\textbf{\te{ఒంటరిగా}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
